test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

I is angry with myself / for making / so many mistakes.
solution:
The erroneous part is: **I is angry with myself.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given compound sentence, the error is with "Helping verb" or "auxiliary verbs".
 
• The part "I** is** angry with myself" has a grammatical error instead of it, the sentence should be " I **am** angry with myself".
 
• For example:
 
 
• I is very happy. (incorrect)
 
• I am very happy. (correct)
 
 
 
• In the sentence "I is angry with myself", the tense used is **Present Continuous Tense.**
 
 
• We know that in Present continuous tense there are three helping verbs - is, am, are.
 
• "I" is singular and first-person pronoun and helping verb "am" is used with the singular first-person pronoun.
 
• Therefore, with the subject "I" we always use "am" as a helping verb.
 
 

Therefore, the correct sentence should be:* I **am** angry with myself.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are the three present tense forms of *to be*.

 
 
• **"Am"** is used with the **first-person**** singular pronoun (I am).**
 
• **"is"** is used with the **third person singular pronoun (**For example**-he is, she is, it is)** and
 
• **"are*****"** *is used with-
 
 
• the **first-person**** plural **pronoun **(**For example-**we are)**
 
• the **second person singular** and** plural **pronoun **(**For example-**you are)**
 
• the **third person plural **pronoun **(**For example-**they are)**.
